a_summary: Azure Monitor collects metrics and logs from your own resources so you can see performance and set alerts.
b_summary: Azure Service Health reports on platform issues, such as outages and planned maintenance, that affect your Azure services.
a_use_when: You want to see how your own apps and virtual machines are performing.
b_use_when: You want to know whether an Azure outage or planned maintenance is affecting your region.

a_summary: Azure Policy checks resources against rules about configuration, such as allowed regions or required tags.
b_summary: Role-based access control decides which users can perform which actions on Azure resources.
a_use_when: You want to enforce rules on how resources are configured.
b_use_when: You want to control who can create, change or delete resources.

a_summary: A resource lock prevents accidental deletion or modification of a resource, even by users who have permission.
b_summary: Role-based access control grants or limits what each user can do on resources, but does not protect resources from changes by authorised users.
a_use_when: You want to protect an important resource from accidental deletion or changes.
b_use_when: You want to decide which people or groups can manage resources.

a_summary: Microsoft Entra ID is the cloud identity service that manages user accounts and verifies who people are when they sign in.
b_summary: Role-based access control decides what a signed-in user is allowed to do on Azure resources.
a_use_when: You need to manage user accounts, sign-in and authentication methods.
b_use_when: You need to decide what a signed-in user can access or change.
